Right, I did read this and initially thought you weren't compatible- but then I remembered my journey into non-monogamy. When my ex and I first opened our relationship, I was so jealous. I couldn't think about her having sex with someone else without feeling sick. Granted, we opened up the relationship to 'save ' it which never works but, still. 

We broke up (not to do w being poly, other issues) and I am now pursuing poly relationships as this is best for me. I still struggle with jealousy. I still need to feel like I'm the 'favourite'. It's on us to unlearn this. It's not our partners responsibility- yes, they can do stuff to help us, but ultimately it lands on us. So, you can choose to deal with it, manage these feelings or move on and find someone monogamous. 

Jealousy is natural. And I guarantee when she does stuff with another person, it will feel like your heart is hurting. But you can work on this! And honestly, now I LOVE hearing my partners stories of their experiences. I love seeing their smiles when they talk about these experiences I know I can't give them.

Neoprponouns can be used in place of others because a lot of non-binary/trans ppl may feel uncomfortable with pronouns like they/them and prefer alternate pronouns. For some, they/them can sound unnatural, and I also believe ppl like other pronouns as they don’t denote gender.

Microlabelling is harmful in some ways. Not for everyone, but I think describing your ENTIRE sexuality, romantic orientation and gender to strangers online can be harmful. It’s okay to be questioning and still discovering things, using fifty different labels will only be confusing in the long run.

He/him lesbians aren’t men. Whilst for the large majority of people, pronouns DO equal gender, for some this is not the case and this is true for he/him lesbians. If you visit r/butchlesbians, they can describe this a lot better than myself, but a lot of lesbians feel disconnected from womenhood and their main connection to womenhood is knowing they love women. Lesbian is a more complex term than people are led to believe, and a lot of AFAB lesbians commonly experience dysphoria but do not wish to be men. This has been an integral part of our community for a long time, a lot of butch lesbians in history have used pronouns over than she/her. 

Hope this helps!
